result:
Solution 2 is wrong. Its premise that $H^3(\Gamma_{0,3}^+(p);\mathbb{Q})$ equals the weight-2 cusp forms on $\Gamma_0(p)$ has no justification, and its vanishing list is also off: $X_0(p)$ has genus 0 for $p=2,3,5,7,13$, so the "$p\ge 11$" claim fails. Solution 1's orbit analysis is sloppy, and its conclusion that only $p=2$ gives vanishing is not supported by a valid computation. I could not verify the full Steinberg-coinvariant computation here.

Solution 3 cites the Miller–Patzt–Putman work on top-dimensional cohomology of congruence subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$, which I recall as giving vanishing for $n=3$ exactly at $p\in\{2,3,5\}$. That recollection is from memory, not checked against the paper, so my confidence is moderate. Solution 3 is the most plausible of the three, and its sum $2+3+5=10$ is the one I would take as correct.

CHOICE: 3
